:::{#cor-normal-density-precision}
#### The Gaussian density in terms of the precision

If $X$ has the [Gaussian distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-normal) $\ndist{\mean, \ss}$,
and $\precision = 1 / \ss$,
then $\precision$ is the [precision](variance-covariance.qmd#def-precision) of $X$,
and $X$ has [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf):

$$
\p(X = x) = \sqrt{\frac{\precision}{2\pi}} \ef{-\frac{\precision}{2} (x - \mean)^2}, \quad x \in \reals.
$$

:::

::: proof

By @exm-mvn-univariate, $X$ is the case $p = 1$ of the [multivariate Gaussian distribution](#def-mvn), with $\matr{\covmat} = (\ss)$.
By [the mean and variance of the Gaussian distribution](random-variables.qmd#thm-normal-moments), $\Var{X} = \ss$,
so the [precision](variance-covariance.qmd#def-precision) of $X$ is $1 / \ss = \precision$.
By @thm-precision-matrix-inverse, the [precision matrix](#def-precision-matrix) of $X$ is the $1 \times 1$ [inverse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-matrix-inverse) of $(\ss)$,
which is $\matr{\Lambda} = (\precision)$,
so by @thm-mvn-density-precision with $p = 1$:

$$
\ba
\p(X = x)
&= \frac{\precision^{1/2}}{(2\pi)^{1/2}} \ef{-\frac{1}{2} (x - \mean) \precision (x - \mean)}
&& \text{(substitute into the precision form)} \\
&= \sqrt{\frac{\precision}{2\pi}} \ef{-\frac{\precision}{2} (x - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

:::
